coverage.evidence: race.py wraps optimizer:_multi_start_minimize with mock.patch.object. For every call it records objective, candidates, bounds, args (the fixed DHW schedule), maxiter, batch_objective, fd_eps and the returned x. Challengers replay production's own jac path (_batch_fd_gradient where _bounds_supported_by_batch holds). Every plan is scored on the exact captured objective. coord.py captures the same seam through a real HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_run_optimization cycle, with _await_optimize patched to run optimize_in_process inline.

Per captured call the challengers were: a tight polish (ftol 1e-12, gtol 1e-9, maxiter 3000, maxfun 1e6); every production candidate refined alone through the real seam; 13 bang-bang anchors at 0 to 3.0x production's own baseline-thermostat energy (hooked at HeatPumpOptimizer._compute_baseline_power), each refined alone; then a warm-start tight polish of the best one. Two A/B harnesses change one production input each: seeds_ab.py (the DHW path's seed set) and stoprule_ab.py (ftol 1e-6 -> 1e-9, with nit/nfev counts). No global outer bound was run (see unfinished).

A challenger counts only if its floor and ceiling breach (degree-steps outside 17-23 C, summed over room for single-zone and upper+lower zones for two-zone, the zones the objective scores) is no worse than production's plus 0.01. On the DHW path the DHW schedule is a fixed argument of the captured call, and the minimum DHW temperature printed by every A/B pair is identical. Power bounds are the captured bounds. Result: cells_feasibility_worse=0 on every seed arm and 3 on the ftol arm.

The shipped 24 h horizon over 4 winter prices x 5 weathers x {single, two-zone} x {DHW on, off} = 80 cells (race.py): gap max 0.5340 %, mean 0.0767 %, 20 cells over 0.1 %. Coordinator captures: 4 configs x 4 prices = 16 cells (coord.py), max 0.1552 %. 6 h and 48 h runs on a 6-cell subset. Valve and wood topologies were not swept, and the 6/48 h runs cover only the subset (see unfinished).

findings.title: The two-zone 0.20x deep anchor is built only in _optimize_space_only; the DHW path's _solve_space never gets it
findings.claim: The DHW path, which every default install runs, builds its own cold-start seed set in HeatPumpOptimizer._solve_space, and that set does not include the two-zone 0.20x baseline-energy anchor. Adding that anchor lowers the shipped objective on two-zone DHW-on winter cells by up to 0.2507 % (0.3396 objective units per day). The paired flat-price cells show 0.0000 %.
findings.mechanism: _optimize_space_only seeds from the baseline thermostat: its power, plus bang-bang anchors at 1.0x and 0.35x of its energy, plus 0.20x for two-zone houses. _solve_space seeds instead from init_base: an init_base-shaped guess, bang-bang at init_base energy, headroom*0.5, and bang-bang at 0.35x init_base energy. So the DHW path has no baseline-power seed, keys its anchors on a different energy, and never gets the 0.20x under-heat anchor that round 7 found the price-driven two-zone optimum needs.

findings.claim: In 3 of 3 auth-refusal arms (setup 401, setup 403, steady-cycle 401), the exception the integration delivers is transient-class (ConfigEntryNotReady or UpdateFailed), not ConfigEntryAuthFailed. findings.mechanism: _fetch_tibber_prices calls _tibber_start_reauth on a 'reauth' verdict, then _tibber_fetch_failed raises UpdateFailed. The stub has no ConfigEntryAuthFailed class and no auth arm in DataUpdateCoordinator._async_refresh, so no test can express the correct behaviour (P11).

findings.title: Euler sub-step guard judges each store's diagonal ratio only, so coupled stores in accepted configs diverge
findings.claim: For configurations the config flow accepts, ThermalModel._stability_substeps leaves the per-substep Euler map with spectral radius > 1, and a zero-input 24 h trajectory diverges (69/3936 grid configs leave the passive envelope, 50 past 100 K; named point reaches -2.84e35 degC).
findings.mechanism: _stability_substeps bounds each store's (sum of couplings)/C*h by EULER_STABILITY_MAX_RATIO=1.5, on the premise that Euler is stable up to 2 per store. For coupled RC stores the stiff eigenvalue reaches the sum of the diagonal terms (Gershgorin: |lambda| <= 2*max diag), so lambda*h reaches 3 and the update oscillates with growth. Example: house mass 0.5, loss 0.2, slab mass 0.5, slab transfer 5.0 -> n_sub=2, radius 1.525.

findings.title: DHW refill coil debits the wood tank the full coil heat but spares the DHW tank only its scaled share

findings.title: A malformed weather-forecast response wedges every later cycle until restart
findings.claim: One weather.get_forecasts response whose forecast holds a non-dict row or is not a list makes every later _async_update_data raise UpdateFailed, even after the weather entity returns a healthy forecast again.

findings.claim: The EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener from async_register_worker_shutdown, fired 0.1 s into a real solve, returns only when the solve does (0.93 of the solve's duration), against 0.008 s with no solve in flight.

findings.title: Settlement caps (slab_settlement_cap, hold_demand_kw) ignore the learned house_heat_loss_scale the dynamics apply
findings.claim: optimizer.slab_settlement_cap and optimizer.hold_demand_kw size the steady-state demand from the raw zone losses. simulate_step multiplies those losses by house_heat_loss_scale (via effective_heat_loss_coefficient), and the sibling _buffer_charge_ceiling does the same. So at any learned scale other than 1, the 'sustaining' slab cap does not sustain the target: the room drifts at up to 1.44 K/h, the cap sits up to 13.5 K low (67.5 kWh of slab heat the terminal cost cannot see), and published predicted_savings are overstated by up to 13.4 currency at scale 2.
findings.mechanism: slab_settlement_cap: q_demand = u*(target-out) - gains, with u = heat_loss_coefficient or lower_floor_heat_loss_learned and no house_heat_loss_scale. hold_demand_kw has the same omission. Both feed _settlement_caps, which feeds _terminal_cost (the objective) and _deferred_energy_cost (the published savings). The dynamics and _buffer_charge_ceiling (the latter explicitly: 'a learned-leaky house that omitted it here got an optimistic ceiling') apply the scale.

findings.title: #1067 flow-lift bias clamp (15 K) cannot reach real supply: model curve tops out at 27.9 C, COP overstated up to 37%
findings.claim: With flow_curve_cop enabled, ThermalModel.compute_cop prices the direct-plant lift at curve_flow_temp + flow_curve_bias. The model's own curve never exceeds 27.9 C on the default houses, because emitter UA is derived from pump nameplate at a fixed 15 K, while the bias is clamped at FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K = 15 K. So a plant running at 40/45/50 C pins the bias at the clamp in every cell, and the priced COP exceeds the COP at the real supply by up to 8.4% / 22.8% / 36.8%.
findings.mechanism: flow_lift.FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K is justified in its comment against a 35 C curve ('a fixed-setpoint plant running 45 C against a curve asking 35 C is 10 K out'). But curve_supply_temp -> flow_target_for_indoor -> mixing_valve.flow_setpoint uses emitter_ua = max_electrical_power*cop_nominal/emitter_design_delta_t (15 K, not configurable), which gives 22-28 C curves. Residuals of 17-27 K are real installation offsets against this curve, but the clamp truncates them.

The flag is off by default, so no golden fixture moves except direct_flow_carnot if it enables the curve.

findings.title: A tz-less return_time (card datetime-local) or a naive stored datetime wedges every cycle with TypeError
findings.claim: A set_away return_time without an offset (the card's <input type=datetime-local> value, and services.yaml's own example) makes away.expire_override compare naive with aware; every later solve then returns solve_failed (2 of 2), and _resolve_away raises on 6 of 6 cycles, until away is switched off.
findings.mechanism: away._parse_return_time returns datetime.fromisoformat(value) unnormalised. async_set_away stores the naive ISO string before expire_override raises, so every coordinator._resolve_away inside async_run_optimization raises and is fenced into 'solve_failed' with an ERROR traceback. The same unnormalised parse sits in legionella async_load (dt_util.parse_datetime, consumed by async_track's now - previous), in pump_arbiter._load (datetime.fromisoformat, consumed by hold()'s now - at, which escapes _apply_action as UpdateFailed) and in boost._parse_until (restore raises once). manual_plan._coerce_awareness is the sibling seam that guards it.

findings.title: Pump-duty arbiter re-registers its timer and state listener on an unloaded coordinator and keeps writing the pump
findings.claim: A pump state change dispatched just before unload leaves 2 live arbiter registrations on the torn-down coordinator after async_shutdown, and the leaked 1-minute tick writes the pump (2 writes) after the unload.
findings.mechanism: pump_arbiter._changed queues hass.async_create_task(apply(coord)). async_shutdown -> pump_arbiter.release -> release_listeners empties held.unsubs. The queued apply then runs; it never checks coord._entry_released, and _listen sees empty unsubs, so it registers async_track_time_interval(_tick, 1 min) and async_track_state_change_event again. Nothing unsubscribes them, so the dead instance commands the pump every minute alongside the reloaded one, or after the integration is disabled.

findings.title: Hot water without a tank probe: every solve starts from the 55 C ThermalState default, never advanced
findings.claim: With hot water configured and dhw_temp_entity omitted (the config flow's default install), the coordinator hands the solver dhw_temperature = 55.0 C on every cycle. In a 24-cycle closed loop, 23 of 24 solves start more than 1 K away from the tank the integration's own model says it left, and the model-truth tank spends 6.25 h of the demand windows below dhw_min_temperature, against 0 h with the probe mapped.
findings.mechanism: coordinator._update_current_state writes _current_state.dhw_temperature only from an ok reading of CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY (coordinator.py ~5431), and no other producer advances it. So _solve_snapshot deep-copies the ThermalState dataclass default of 55.0 into every solve, and the optimizer uses initial_state.dhw_temperature as the tank's initial temperature. The plan therefore always believes the tank was just charged, schedules little DHW, and the next cycle resets to 55 again. _dhw_probe_temperature already fences this constant away from the display and the learners, but the solver is not fenced. slab_temperature is the same seam when floor_return_temp_entity is omitted: it is seeded once to room+1 K and never advanced (1 distinct solver-initial value in 24 solves, against 23-24 with the probe).

findings.title: DefrostDerate.from_dict admits non-finite/out-of-range duty; the bucket pins at DERATE_MIN and never recovers

findings.title: On an on/off pump, the switch path switches off steps whose planned heat the plan books as delivered
findings.claim: The solver treats a step below the modulation floor as duty cycling within the step (bounds [0,P_max], optimizer.py ~:3962). The switch path instead commands ON only at max(0.1, min_electrical_power*0.5) (HeatPumpOptimizer._power_to_heat_pump_schedule and get_current_action; pump_arbiter._on_kw uses the same threshold). On an on/off pump (min==max==6 kW, which config_flow._power_errors accepts) the threshold is 3 kW, so the plan's 1.0-1.4 kW trickle is switched OFF while the trajectory, cost and savings count that heat as delivered. On/off arm: 4/9 cells withhold more than 10% of planned energy. Shoulder withholds 0.671 (8.30 of 12.38 kWh over 30 steps), producing 30 end-to-end switch.turn_off calls on steps with planned heat. Modulating null arm: 0/9 cells (max 0.014) and 0 such calls. Shoulder open-loop consequence: min room 20.64 C planned vs 19.89 C actuated, 17.2 K*h below the plan's own trajectory, 0 K*h below min_temperature.

findings.title: Climate hvac_action publishes off while an active boost runs the pump in optimizer mode off

findings.title: P2: the two-zone and wood-furnace facts are re-derived from a proxy key at three seams beside their canonical predicate
findings.claim: On 40 boundary configurations, config_flow._derive_preset disagrees with ThermalParameters.from_config(...).two_zone_enabled on 20 and modbus_prefill.infer offers a flow target the pre-fill save refuses (or misses one it would accept) on 20; on 21 wood configurations topology.describe_setup's wood tank disagrees with wood_fuel.wood_furnace_on on 2; each drops to 0 when the proxy read is replaced by the canonical predicate.
findings.mechanism: ThermalParameters.from_config decides two_zone_enabled from the explicit two_zone_mode override first and the presence of any of four zone keys second; wood_fuel.wood_furnace_on decides the furnace from its flag first and a fixed inferred-key set second. Three seams decide the same fact themselves: _derive_preset (config_flow.py:1125) and modbus_prefill._plant (modbus_prefill.py:212) test bool(current.get(CONF_UPPER_FLOOR_THERMAL_MASS)), ignoring the mode key, the other three presence keys and a present-but-0.0 value; topology._wood_tank_shown (topology.py:376) re-derives the furnace from a different inferred-key set (adds valve_outlet_temp_entity, drops dhw_wood_coil_enabled). The R7-D12-01 fix (3602b6ca) moved the flow-target guard and the pre-fill save guard to the canonical predicate and left these siblings. Consequence: a two_zone_mode=off install whose zone keys survive in entry.data gets two-zone questionnaire physics written into a single-zone model (house_thermal_mass 0.267x the canonical preset's on the probe house); two_zone_mode=on without an upper-mass key gets single-zone physics (3.75x); the GCHV pre-fill offers a flow write target its own save then refuses; the setup diagram draws a wood tank the model does not run, or hides one it does.

findings.title: P8: a money figure's currency comes from the label source, never from the price feed that denominates it
findings.claim: Over 12 feed-unit x instance-currency cells the current-price sensor publishes the feed's number under hass.config.currency in all 8 cells where the price entity declares a different ISO code, with no repair issue in any; the firewood price widget is the only one of 4 currency-labelled option widgets that ignores the instance currency; and the card names two currencies on one screen for un-converted figures when card-config currency is set (price axis and what-if delta off the install's currency -- 3 counted surfaces, the axis counted as computed and as drawn; 4 before R7-D4-03, the savings table too).
findings.mechanism: inputs.normalize_price_per_kwh parses a price entity's <money>/<energy> unit for its scale and discards the money code ('The currency itself is never converted'); coordinator.currency is currency.resolve_currency(hass), i.e. hass.config.currency, and every money sensor's native_unit_of_measurement and the plan sensors' currency attribute come from it; _audit_price_units only flags an unparseable unit. So an EUR/kWh Nord Pool entity on an SEK instance publishes 0.10 as 0.10 SEK/kWh. The config flow resolves three money widgets through resolve_currency(hass) but CONF_WOOD_PRICE_SEK_M3's widget hard-codes 'SEK/m³' (config_flow.py:1645; also the simulate_plan service description in strings.json/en/sv), and wood_fuel compares that price directly with the plan's electricity prices. The card resolves currency twice: PlanSource.currency() lets card-config currency lead (price axis, what-if delta), savingsUnit() lets the savings sensor's declared unit lead (headline, savings table) -- R7-D4-03 moved only the savings table.

findings.title: I4: class roster and finding grammar have disagreeing readers (P11 on no D14 seat; intake admits schema-refused ids)
findings.claim: bugclasses.json has 16 class ids but scopes.json's D14 axis has 15, so P11 is held by no D14 seat while check_scopes.check() reports D14 ok; and audit-find.js's intake, executed on 22 boundary findings, admits 11 that finding.schema.json refuses (class ids P0/P12/P99/I0/I6/P011 and ids D14-s2-1/-001/-xx/-/-01a), 0 after it is rebuilt from the ledger and the schema's id pattern.
findings.mechanism: The class roster is written in four places: the ledger (bugclasses.json), the schema enum (held equal to the ledger by check-wave-script.mjs), the D14 axis in scopes.json (held equal to nothing), and audit-find.js's CLASS_GUESS = /^([PI][0-9]+|new)$/ plus a reportSchema whose class_guess is {type: 'string'}. P11 was added to the ledger and the schema (v6.6.12 root cause) but not to the D14 axis, and check_scopes.py proves completeness against the dimension's own axis, which is the stale list. findings.title: Eight production seams still do wall-clock datetime arithmetic across DST; the forecast grid lands 60 min off
findings.claim: On every 2025-2027 Europe/Stockholm transition day the real coordinator cycle executes datetime arithmetic at 9 distinct production sites whose result differs from the UTC truth (8 instances plus tariff._window_slot, a wall-clock label by definition), and the worst (_forecast_arrays' step_offset) puts step 0 of the price/weather grid 60 min away from the solve anchor on 42 of 48 cycles.
findings.mechanism: Home Assistant hands every datetime the process-wide ZoneInfo instance; CPython subtracts two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object as naive wall clock, and datetime+timedelta on a zoned value is wall-clock addition. _forecast_arrays computes step_offset=(now-midnight) in wall minutes, then _utc_step_starts walks UTC from midnight by that many steps, so after the transition the grid is 1 h late (spring) or early (autumn) and the plan is priced against the wrong hour for ~21 h. tests/dst_checks.py freezes only 00:07 (offset 0) so it never runs this path.

findings.title: The replay lane freezes a fixed-offset clock, so a DST-day replay reports zero P7 seams
findings.claim: tests/replay.py:run_fixture replaying a DST transition day lets 0 wrong-duration sites through the P7 tracer, while the same days on the clock Home Assistant provides (ZoneInfo) show 10.
findings.mechanism: run_fixture freezes dt_util.now() at _ts(window.start)+k*step, a datetime.fromisoformat value with a fixed-offset tzinfo that never changes across the day; production arithmetic on it is UTC-correct by construction, so the lane cannot observe the shared-ZoneInfo wall-clock class (and its clock reads the wrong local hour after a transition). The D14 stop rule leans on the nightly replay; a real DST-day export would replay green. Also a test-double-fidelity shape (bugclasses P11).

findings.title: Mutation ratchet inventory cannot see 528 of 2313 production guard seams; a new guard of those shapes raises it by 0
findings.claim: tests/mutation_table.py:candidates() yields no site on 528 of the 2313 guard seams in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer (52 of 1346 early-exit ifs, 246 of 668 clamps, 230 of 299 threshold ternaries). A new undispositioned guard whose test spans two lines therefore raises unpinned_sites by 0 and ratchet_refusal does not refuse, against +1 and refusal for the same guard on one line.
findings.mechanism: Six single-line operators. GUARD_OFF fires only on an if whose test is on one line, whose line starts with 'if ' and ends with ':', and which has no else; that misses multi-line tests (46), elif (3), a trailing comment after the colon (2) and else branches (1). CLAMP_DROP fires only on a bare min/max with exactly 2 args on one line; that misses numpy/math clamps (179), multi-line calls (63) and 3+ args (4). No operator touches a conditional expression's test. At their pre-fix commits, two of the six ledger I1 instances whose defect is a guard line are of an invisible shape: R5 D3-04 #1312 (the ternary len(positives) >= 2, 076f4a35^) and R5 D3-08 #1316 (np.clip in curve_learning._step_down, 6438f8f6^).

findings.title: Now-marker label prints over the measured-now reading on the live default view
findings.claim: On an install that publishes its measured indoor temperature, the chart's 'now' label and the 'now 21.1 °C' reading overlap (13.8x8.6 px glyph boxes at 375 px, ink visibly merged) in the default view, inline and expanded, in 24 of 24 cells.
findings.mechanism: renderChart places text.now-label at (nx+3, plotT+font+1) and text.now-temp at (plotL+6, plotT+font) independently; the default window starts at now so nx ~ plotL. The test rig's planStates omits the measured sensor (withActuals), so no STATES default view draws now-temp. Same property, second seam: the .viewctl reset button over now-label when panned (history_panned, 10 cells of the full grid).

leads.what: The default-view plan states omit the integration's own measured sensors (withActuals), so card_drift/card_browser never render the live default view; D4-s1-05's collision passed every lane for that reason.
The contrast lane measures four fixed sites on fixtures that never produce a status outcome (.cheaper/.dearer/.wi-warn/.confirm), so D4-s1-01 is outside every gate.
Slot and advisor labels reach the card as published strings; whether the backend localizes them for a Swedish UI was not checked (the fixture's are English).
The card prints narrative lines in the language the sensor published, regardless of hass.language; whether the backend follows the UI language was not checked.
